calls.head: Vegas’s power play outclasses Chicago’s
calls.body: On power play, Vegas sits 2nd of 32, at the lethal end of the scale. Chicago is 31st, at the harmless end.
calls.call: Vegas’s power play creates more per 60 than Chicago’s.
calls.cite: Style fingerprint · this season blended with last · 0 and 0 games this season
calls.happened: On power-play expected goals per 60, Vegas had 7.8 per 60 and Chicago 3.7 per 60. Coming in, Vegas was at 8.7 per 60 and Chicago at 6.4 per 60.

calls.head: Vegas rolls four lines; Chicago leans on its top six
calls.body: Vegas ranks 4th of 32 for depth, toward the deep end; Chicago ranks 28th, toward the top-heavy end.
calls.call: Vegas spreads its forward ice time deeper down the lineup than Chicago.

calls.happened: On bottom-six share of forward ice time, Vegas had 43% and Chicago 43%. Coming in, Vegas was at 43% and Chicago at 40%.

VGK.head: We gave Vegas a 73% chance, and Vegas delivered.

CHI.head: We gave Chicago only a 27% chance, and it went the way we feared.

surprises.head: Chicago tried a different line
surprises.body: O. Moore, P. Kane, R. Kantserov played 9:03 together at 5-on-5, a trio that isn’t one of Chicago’s usual lines.
